solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Most unusual storing data in tropical area

indicators.note: something that stores goods holds them inside it, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: rarest means most uncommon
info is short for information, i.e. data

explanation.surface: Some odd collection of records is being kept in the tropics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most unusual' looks like a description of the data, but it is a single superlative that holds the data inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainforest is a dense, wet woodland typical of equatorial regions, so it is a tropical area.

clue.text: Get back on horse-drawn carriage with no end of trouble

indicators.note: having no end of trouble means the final letter of the word trouble is taken away from the carriage

blocks.note: re means on or concerning
a coupé is a closed four-wheeled carriage
the last letter of trouble, the one removed

explanation.surface: Someone retrieves their horse and carriage, minus a little trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The E removed from COUPE is the end of 'trouble'; RE + COUP remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup is to recover money or losses, which is to get them back.

clue.text: I study topless image that's famously representative of its type

indicators.note: without a top means the first letter of the word for image is lost

blocks.note: taken as written
to con is to study or learn by heart
pic is short for picture, an image

explanation.surface: Someone examines a topless picture that has become a classic of its kind.
explanation.walkthrough: PIC loses its top letter to give IC; 'topless' tempts a racier reading but only trims a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iconic is widely recognised as the emblem or classic example of its kind.

clue.text: Party food for a cannibal?

blocks.note: surface reading: a spread of snacks eaten by hand at a gathering
setter's reading: a cannibal's spread would literally be made of fingers

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the literal reading of a buffet named for what you eat with, taken as what you eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A finger buffet is a party meal of small items eaten with the hands, which a cannibal would read as a menu of digits.

clue.text: Thatcher's material heartlessly delivered

indicators.note: without a heart means the whole middle of the word is cut out, leaving only its ends

blocks.note: redeemed means saved or delivered, as from sin

explanation.surface: Something about the delivery of Margaret Thatcher's speeches lacking heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thatcher' suggests the prime minister; here it is a roofer working with straw or reeds. Several words for delivered (rescued, released) give the same ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeds are dried stems used to thatch roofs, so they are a thatcher's raw material.

clue.text: Press people plot to divide petitioners

indicators.note: dividing something means splitting it apart with the other word placed in the gap

blocks.note: suitors are people who petition or sue
a plot of garden is a bed

explanation.surface: A conspiracy sets a group of petitioners against one another.
explanation.walkthrough: SU(BED)ITORS. 'Plot' suggests a scheme but is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Subeditors work on newspapers checking and editing copy, so they are journalists of the press.

clue.text: Reports heard or herd in Africa?

indicators.note: something heard is taken in by ear, so we want a word that sounds like reports

blocks.note: reports are news, which sounds like the plural animal

explanation.surface: A playful heard/herd confusion about animals on the African plains.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent G makes the antelope sound exactly like reports of events.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnus, or wildebeest, are antelope that roam the African savanna in large herds.

clue.text: VIPs and what they hate to hear when booking dinner

definitions.text: what they hate to hear when booking dinner

blocks.note: first meaning: important or eminent people

blocks.clueFragment: what they hate to hear when booking dinner
blocks.note: second meaning: split as two words, a restaurant saying it is full

explanation.surface: Celebrities dread being told a restaurant is fully booked.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as NO TABLES, the second half is the dreaded phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Notables are prominent people, the same sort as very important persons.

clue.text: Disturbances at university interrupting Arab leaders in speech

indicators.note: in speech means as the words are spoken, so a word sounding like the Arab leaders is wanted
interrupting means breaking into the middle, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: sheikhs are Arab chiefs, pronounced like the word for jolts
up means in residence at university

explanation.surface: Student unrest breaks into speeches by Arab rulers.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAKE(UP)S: the sound-alike of sheikhs is split around UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Shake-ups are radical reorganisations that disrupt the existing order.

clue.text: Top horse race in China

blocks.note: the crown is the top of the head or of a hill
the Derby is the famous English flat race at Epsom

explanation.surface: The best horse race held in the People's Republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country but is porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Crown Derby is a well-known make of English porcelain, which is fine china.

clue.text: Tailless weasel-like mammal in covered walkway

indicators.note: without its tail means the final letter of the animal's name is dropped

blocks.note: the stoat is a small weasel-like animal

explanation.surface: A docked stoat wanders along a colonnade.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a classical Greek portico, a roofed colonnade used as a walkway.

clue.text: Angry representative sample?

blocks.note: surface reading: a sample typical of the whole
setter's reading: a section of people who are cross

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the phrase is also read literally as a section that is in a bad temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-section is a sample typical of a whole population, and cross is a synonym for angry.

clue.text: Soccer team in one of the UAE capitals?

blocks.note: first meaning: a common football club name, as in Manchester or Leeds
second meaning: the word one capital letter of the acronym stands for

explanation.walkthrough: 'Capitals' suggests Abu Dhabi and the like, but means the capital letters of UAE; its U stands for this word.
explanation.definitionFit: United is a familiar football club name and also the first word of United Arab Emirates.

clue.text: Very pleasing girl, outwardly competent

indicators.note: outwardly means on the outside, so one word wraps round the other

blocks.note: able means capable or competent
Dora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl who is charming and seems capable on the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outwardly competent' reads as a description of the girl; in fact the word for competent wraps round her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable means delightful or lovable, very pleasing to see.

clue.text: Fuss manufacturer's understood, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the words are to be said out and matched by sound

blocks.note: a manufacturer is a maker, and understood is seen, as in I see

explanation.surface: A complaint that a manufacturer's position has been grasped, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a scene is to cause a public commotion, which is to make a fuss; here the verb is the sense.

clue.text: Attractive result of going undercover before midnight?

definitions.text: Attractive result of going undercover before midnight?

blocks.note: surface reading: working as a secret agent

blocks.clueFragment: Attractive result of going undercover before midnight?
blocks.note: setter's reading: getting under the bedclothes early, said to keep you looking good

explanation.walkthrough: 'Undercover' suggests spying; here it means under the covers of a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying holds that rest taken before midnight improves your looks, so such early sleep is named for good looks.

clue.text: Proceeds to upset grannies

indicators.note: upsetting something knocks it over and out of order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something goes ahead and bothers the old ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proceeds' reads as a verb but is the noun, money taken in.
explanation.definitionFit: Proceeds are money received from a sale or activity, which is income or earnings.

clue.text: Man showing up in challenge is a poet

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word is read from bottom to top
in places the first word inside the second

blocks.note: a dare is a challenge
a man is a male

explanation.surface: A man rises to a challenge and turns out to be a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'showing up' turns the word upwards. Walter de la Mare wrote 'The Listeners'.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter de la Mare was an English poet, author of 'The Listeners'.

clue.text: This one chose after shuffle?

indicators.note: shuffling a pack mixes the cards up, so these letters are rearranged too

blocks.note: a means one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A card trick: the card you picked after the deck was shuffled.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'This', which the rest of the clue completes: the card picked after shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: The ace of hearts is a playing card, the kind of card picked in a trick after a shuffle.

clue.text: Revolutionary republic defends volunteers of another Arabian state

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning round, so the republic is spelt backwards
defending something means surrounding and protecting it, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: Iraq is a republic in the Middle East
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A revolutionary state protects its volunteer fighters from a neighbour.
explanation.walkthrough: IRAQ reversed is QARI, which surrounds TA: QA(TA)RI.
explanation.definitionFit: Qatari is the adjective for Qatar, a Gulf state on the Arabian peninsula distinct from Iraq.

clue.text: English novelist putting area first for excellence

indicators.note: first for means the opening letter of the following word is taken

blocks.note: a golf green is the area where players putt
opening letter of excellence

explanation.surface: A writer is put at the top of the list for quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting area first' looks like a single instruction; 'putting area' is the golf green and 'first for excellence' gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene was an English writer of novels such as 'Brighton Rock'.

clue.text: Name region engulfed in foremost of endlessly sectarian turmoil

definitions.text: Name region engulfed in foremost of endlessly sectarian turmoil

indicators.note: foremost means at the very front, so the opening letters of the following words are taken
something engulfed is swallowed up and surrounded by something else

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
the opening letters of these three words
an area is a region

explanation.surface: A troubled part of the world caught in unending religious strife.
explanation.walkthrough: N, then E(AREA)ST. 'Region' does double duty: it supplies AREA and defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Near East is a geographical region, the countries of the eastern Mediterranean and southwest Asia.

clue.text: Cake for comedian Jenny?

blocks.note: first meaning: a long cream-filled pastry with chocolate icing
second meaning: the surname of a British stand-up comic

explanation.walkthrough: Jenny Éclair is a British stand-up comedian and broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: An éclair is a choux pastry cake, and the comic took the same word as her stage surname.

clue.text: Movie company that's had a change of direction

indicators.text: that's had a change of direction
indicators.note: a change of direction swaps one direction letter, right for left, inside the word

blocks.note: a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: A film studio that has changed its creative direction.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) in FIRM becomes L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: A film is a motion picture, the same thing as a movie.

clue.text: It's tidy in the old Bull

blocks.note: first meaning: orderly and trim
second meaning: an archaic word for an ox or bovine animal

explanation.walkthrough: The capital B suggests a pub named the Old Bull; the word is an obsolete term for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat means orderly and tidy, and in old English it also named a bovine animal such as an ox.

clue.text: Just hurry on in front of one partner

blocks.note: to leg it is to run off quickly
I is the Roman numeral one
a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: Simply rush ahead of someone's other half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'only' but is the adjective, fair. To leg it is British slang for to run.
explanation.definitionFit: Legitimate means lawful or justifiable, so a just claim is a valid one.

clue.text: Garden feature stood out unusually in leaves

indicators.note: leaves is the verb, departs, so the word in goes out of the longer word

blocks.note: shined, a rare past form of shine, means stood out
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Something in the garden was remarkable among the foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' suggests foliage in a garden, but it is the verb: IN departs SHINED. 'Unusually' marks shined as a less common form than shone.
explanation.definitionFit: A shed is a small hut for tools found in many gardens.

clue.text: You could find me bust, with a new ring in hock?

definitions.note: the answer is the category; hock is one example of it

indicators.note: something bust is broken apart, so these letters are smashed and put back in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A broke speaker has pawned a newly bought ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' and 'in hock' both suggest being broke and pawning things; hock is also the English name for white wine from the Rhine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hock is a white wine from Germany's Rhineland, so it is an example of German wine.
